summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with severe diastolic heart failure, aortic stenosis, atrial fibrillation, and a PleurX catheter for recurrent pleural effusions was admitted for worsening shortness of breath, cough with green sputum, and significant weight gain. He had missed two weeks of outpatient IV lasix due to hypotension and a URI. On admission, he had atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, an elevated INR of 5.5, acute kidney injury, and radiographic findings of a moderate right pleural effusion with atelectasis and new opacity concerning for pneumonia. He was treated with IV lasix for three days, transitioned to oral torsemide 40mg twice daily, and received levofloxacin for community-acquired pneumonia. The PleurX catheter was drained of 3 liters of fluid, improving his respiratory status. Warfarin was held initially and restarted on a adjusted schedule; INR normalized by discharge. Metoprolol was restarted and digoxin added for rate control. His kidney function and leukocytosis resolved, and repeat imaging showed significant improvement. He was discharged home with home health services, on a revised medication regimen including digoxin and continued PleurX drainage three times weekly, with instructions for daily weight monitoring and an INR check the following day.
